question: Is pembrolizumab in any Phase 3 lung cancer trials, and what are its common adverse reactions?

route.reason: The question asks whether pembrolizumab appears in Phase 3 lung cancer trials (registry data) and also asks for its common adverse reactions (drug label data).

draft.text: Yes. ClinicalTrials.gov lists 144 Phase 3 studies matching pembrolizumab and lung cancer [count:1]. Examples: NCT01905657, Pembrolizumab (MK-3475) two doses vs docetaxel in previously treated NSCLC (KEYNOTE-010), Phase 2/3, Completed [trial:NCT01905657]; NCT03302234, Pembrolizumab with ipilimumab or placebo in untreated metastatic NSCLC (KEYNOTE-598), Phase 3, Completed [trial:NCT03302234]; NCT06561386, Nivolumab and relatlimab plus chemotherapy vs pembrolizumab plus chemotherapy in stage IV/recurrent non-squamous NSCLC, Phase 3, Recruiting [trial:NCT06561386]. Common adverse reactions (reported in ≥20% of patients) with KEYTRUDA as a single agent were fatigue, musculoskeletal pain, rash, diarrhea, pyrexia, cough, decreased appetite, pruritus, dyspnea, constipation, pain, abdominal pain, nausea, and hypothyroidism [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0]. With chemotherapy or chemoradiotherapy, common reactions included fatigue/asthenia, nausea, constipation, diarrhea, decreased appetite, rash, vomiting, cough, dyspnea, pyrexia, alopecia, and peripheral neuropathy, among others [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0]. The label also describes severe and fatal immune-mediated adverse reactions and infusion-related reactions [label:pembrolizumab:adverse_reactions:0].
